alt: A word is shown one character per cell with its positive indices under the cells. A pointer moves to word[0], the first character, then to word[-1], the last, then to word[-len(word)], which lands on the first character again. A final pointer sits past the last cell at index 10, where no character exists, so Python raises IndexError. Presets use a seven-letter word and a three-letter word.

steps.caption: The word "pumpkin" has 7 characters. Indexing reads one of them by position, and the positions run from 0 to 6.
`word[0]` is "p". Positions start at 0, so index 0 is the first character.
`word[-1]` is "n". A negative index counts back from the end, so -1 is always the last character, index 6 here.
`word[-7]` is "p", the same character as `word[0]`. -7 is -len(word), the furthest back an index can go.
`word[10]` points past the last index, 6. No character is there, so Python raises `IndexError` instead of returning anything.
The word "cat" has 3 characters. Indexing reads one of them by position, and the positions run from 0 to 2.
`word[0]` is "c". Positions start at 0, so index 0 is the first character.
`word[-1]` is "t". A negative index counts back from the end, so -1 is always the last character, index 2 here.
`word[-3]` is "c", the same character as `word[0]`. -3 is -len(word), the furthest back an index can go.
`word[10]` points past the last index, 2. No character is there, so Python raises `IndexError` instead of returning anything.
